trip.title: The UAE Story — Heritage, Innovation & Adventure
trip.city: Dubai, Sharjah, Abu Dhabi, Al Ain & Ras Al Khaimah
overview: This seven-day multi-emirate programme is built as an immersive introduction to the United Arab Emirates, linking history, culture, geography, sustainability, architecture, innovation and outdoor learning. Students follow the country as a connected story: the coastal and desert communities that came first, the formation and rapid development of the nation, and the ideas now shaping its future. Educational themes include UAE history and national identity, Islamic culture and architecture, desert environments, archaeology and early settlement, sustainable cities, science and technology, art and global cultures, traditional crafts, water management and oases, mountain geology and responsible tourism.

The route moves from Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, Dubai Creek and the Etihad Museum to Expo City Dubai and the Museum of the Future, then on to Sharjah and the desert archaeology of Mleiha, the capital's Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque and Qasr Al Watan, Louvre Abu Dhabi and Qasr Al Hosn, the oasis landscape of Al Ain, and finally Dhayah Fort and Jebel Jais in Ras Al Khaimah. Guided educational visits are deliberately balanced with practical fieldwork and reflection time, and the same itinerary can be reframed for History, Geography, Design & Technology, Art, Business, Islamic Studies, Global Perspectives, Environmental Science or Citizenship.

Suggested for students aged 11–18 and adaptable by curriculum, age group and season. A practical routing is four nights in Dubai and two nights in Abu Dhabi, with the Al Ain excursion operating from Abu Dhabi. The programme is full board, with group menus agreed in advance and halal, vegetarian, vegan, allergy-aware and medically required options confirmed before travel. Private air-conditioned coach transport is used throughout with seat belts and licensed drivers. All visits should be risk-assessed for the age and needs of the group; students remain under school supervision throughout and supplier-led activities should be checked against school safeguarding and insurance requirements. Timed-entry attractions and workshops are subject to opening schedules, school-group capacity and advance confirmation, with equivalent educational alternatives used where needed.

itinerary_days.label: Day 4
itinerary_days.title: Abu Dhabi — Faith, Leadership & Nationhood
itinerary_days.description: Following breakfast and check-out, the group travels to the federal capital for a guided cultural tour of Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, examining geometry, calligraphy, materials and symmetry alongside religious practice and the values of hospitality and respect; appropriate dress and visitor etiquette are discussed before arrival. After a group lunch, students visit Qasr Al Watan, the working Presidential palace, to discuss the institutions of the UAE, scholarship, diplomacy and national development, comparing its architectural language with that of the mosque. The afternoon includes time on the Corniche and waterfront, followed by dinner in Abu Dhabi and an evening reflection on the character of a capital city.
itinerary_days.summary: Abu Dhabi's civic identity read through two buildings: the Grand Mosque's geometry and calligraphy, and a working Presidential palace devoted to governance and scholarship.

itinerary_days.label: Day 1
itinerary_days.title: Dubai — From Creek to Union
itinerary_days.description: A guided walk through Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood introduces wind-tower architecture and life before air conditioning and oil wealth, prompting discussion of how climate, materials, family life and trade shaped the early city. The group then crosses Dubai Creek by traditional abra and explores the old trading districts and souks, learning about merchants, pearling, maritime connections and migration. After lunch in Old Dubai, a visit to the Etihad Museum examines the leadership, negotiation and shared vision behind the union of 1971. The day closes with a panoramic introduction to modern Dubai and a welcome dinner, with a short reflection on the speed of change.
itinerary_days.summary: Wind-tower lanes, an abra crossing and the souks of old Dubai set up the story of pearling, trade and the 1971 union.

itinerary_days.label: Day 3
itinerary_days.title: Sharjah — Culture Beneath the Sand
itinerary_days.description: A guided visit to the Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilization, or a comparable heritage programme, explores the contribution of Islamic civilisation to art, science, navigation, architecture and learning, while time in the historic city shows how conservation protects traditional urban character. After lunch in the Sharjah or Mleiha area, the group travels inland to Mleiha Archaeological Centre to study evidence of early inhabitants, burial sites and geological formations, investigating how climate, water, movement and trade influenced settlement. A guided desert component allows students to read rock formations, dunes, wadis and plains before returning to Dubai for dinner.
itinerary_days.summary: Islamic civilisation's achievements in science and navigation set against Mleiha's prehistoric burial sites, where desert geology reveals why early people settled here.

itinerary_days.label: Day 5
itinerary_days.title: Abu Dhabi — Art, Identity & Living Heritage
itinerary_days.description: The morning is spent at Louvre Abu Dhabi on Saadiyat Island, exploring connections between civilisations, artistic traditions and belief systems, with the building offering a case study in architecture, light, geometry and environmental design; the visit can be tailored towards art, history, design, languages or global citizenship. After lunch on Saadiyat or in central Abu Dhabi, the group visits Qasr Al Hosn and the neighbouring House of Artisans to encounter traditional crafts such as Al Sadu weaving and palm-frond work, with a demonstration or hands-on workshop where available. Dinner in Abu Dhabi is followed by discussion of why cultural preservation matters in a rapidly changing society.
itinerary_days.summary: Louvre Abu Dhabi's cross-cultural galleries and luminous dome set against the city's oldest fort and workshops keeping Emirati crafts alive.

itinerary_days.label: Day 6
itinerary_days.title: Al Ain — The Oasis City
itinerary_days.description: The group travels inland to Al Ain, where Al Ain Oasis and its traditional falaj irrigation systems provide a practical lesson in managing scarce water in an arid environment, linking date cultivation, groundwater and settlement. A visit to Al Jahili Fort, or another suitable heritage site, explores the defensive and administrative role of forts in the oasis. After lunch in Al Ain, the group heads to the Jebel Hafit landscape to consider geology, early settlement and long-distance trade, with viewpoints revealing the contrast between oasis, desert plain and mountain terrain. The return to Dubai is followed by dinner on arrival.
itinerary_days.summary: Falaj channels, date gardens and a desert fort reveal how water, defence and trade shaped settlement, before Jebel Hafit's geology and viewpoints.

itinerary_days.label: Day 2
itinerary_days.title: Dubai — Designing the Future
itinerary_days.description: The morning is spent at Expo City Dubai, where Terra – The Sustainability Pavilion uses interactive exhibits and school-focused learning to explore energy, water, consumption and biodiversity, with the building itself serving as a case study in sustainable architecture. After lunch at Expo City or a nearby group venue, and subject to advance school-group availability, the Museum of the Future frames enquiry into science, technology, health, space and climate, encouraging students to question which innovations genuinely solve problems. The group then visits Downtown Dubai to consider urban planning and scale against the backdrop of Burj Khalifa, with dinner in the Downtown area.

itinerary_days.label: Day 7
itinerary_days.title: Ras Al Khaimah — Mountains, Forts & Farewell
itinerary_days.description: Travelling north to Ras Al Khaimah, the group visits the hilltop Dhayah Fort, where the relationship between geography and defence is clear, and discusses why settlements developed where water and fertile land were available. After lunch in the Ras Al Khaimah or Jebel Jais area, students view the Hajar Mountain scenery from a suitable viewing area and, subject to weather, age and risk-assessment requirements, join a guided low-intensity nature or geology walk examining rock, elevation, temperature, erosion and mountain habitats. The group returns to Dubai for a farewell dinner and guided reflection, which may include student presentations or a travel journal activity.
